title: Vanilla Panna Cotta
description: Barely set cream flecked with vanilla, with just enough gelatine to hold a gentle wobble when turned out. Ten minutes of work, then the fridge does the rest.

items.note: standard supermarket leaves, about 5g in total
a few drops for the moulds

steps.text: Put the gelatine leaves in a bowl of cold water, making sure they are fully submerged, and leave to soften for 5 minutes. Very lightly oil four 150ml ramekins or dariole moulds with a piece of kitchen paper.

Put the cream, milk, sugar and vanilla in a saucepan over a medium-low heat. Warm, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is steaming with small bubbles at the edge. Take it off the heat before it boils.
steps.tip: Boiling is unnecessary and can weaken the set. Steaming hot is all you need to dissolve the gelatine.

steps.text: Lift the gelatine out of the water and squeeze it firmly to get rid of the excess. Drop it into the hot cream and stir for a minute until it has completely dissolved.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a jug. Leave it to cool for 15 minutes, stirring once or twice, so the vanilla seeds stay suspended and do not all sink to the bottom.
Stir once more, pour into the moulds and cover. Chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until set with a gentle wobble.
To turn out, dip each mould into a bowl of hot water for 5–10 seconds, run the tip of a knife around the top edge, then invert onto a plate and give it a firm shake. Serve with the raspberries.
steps.tip: If one refuses to budge, dip it again for a few seconds. Too long in the water and the outside will melt.

tips: Gelatine leaves vary in size and strength between brands. If yours are noticeably larger than about 7 x 11cm, weigh out 5g.
Not confident about turning them out? Set the panna cotta in glasses and serve it as it is.

substitutions.note: infuse the pod in the warm cream and remove it when you strain

substitutions.use: poached rhubarb, roasted plums or a spoonful of berry compote

storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Turn out just before serving. Not suitable for freezing.
author: Simmer
